I have everything I need. Here are the answers.

**h01** — `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`), which re-presigns expiring S3 object URLs on attachments (`CheckAndPresign`, `runner.go:47`; refreshes any URL whose `LastPresignedTime` is older than 4 days of a 5-day expiry, `runner.go:88-91`) — **schedule**: once immediately at startup, then every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`; ticker loop `runner.go:29-41`) — **wiring**: `Server.startBackgroundRunners`, `server/server.go:162-171` (constructed `:162`, immediate `RunOnce` `:163`, goroutine `Run` `:169`), called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

**h02** — **delivery function**: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`, actual HTTP send at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152` (`safeClient.Do(req)`); async path `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`) enqueues onto `asyncPostQueue` drained by 4 worker goroutines in `init()` (`:42-52`) that also call `Post`.
**protection**: SSRF guard at dial time — `safeClient`'s `Transport.DialContext = safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-38`, `:59-77`), which resolves the host and rejects any address in a reserved/private range (defeats DNS rebinding). Ranges + check: `reservedCIDRs`/`isReservedIP` — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`, `:44-53` (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/169.254.169.254 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents). Pre-validation at config time: `webhook.ValidateURL` — `internal/webhook/validate.go:62`, called from `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`. Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`).

**h03** — **abstraction package**: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:3` — `IdentityProviderUserInfo`, the common user-info contract; consumed at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:19,104,119`).
**implementation package**: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20` `IdentityProvider`, `:27` `NewIdentityProvider`, `:44` `ExchangeToken`, `UserInfo`) — OAuth2/OIDC is the only concrete protocol shipped; constructed at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:121`.

**h04** — **no**. Evidence: `grep -rn "mysql\.NewDB" --include="*.go" .` returns exactly one hit, `store/db/db.go:22`, inside the `switch profile.Driver` factory `NewDBDriver` (`store/db/db.go:14-30`). By contrast `sqlite.NewDB` *is* called outside the factory (in tests: `store/demo_seed_test.go:24`, `store/deployment_config_test.go:416`), so the absence for MySQL is not an artifact of the search. The `mysql.*` hits in `store/test/containers.go:42,101-105` are the testcontainers `modules/mysql` package, not `store/db/mysql`.

**h05** — **mechanism: explicit Go code**, in the per-driver `DeleteUser` transaction; there is **no** DB-level cascade for reactions.
Evidence:
- Go deletes: `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96` (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, decl `:380`, `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN …` `:383`) and `:102` (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`, decl `:400`, `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = …` `:401`), both inside `deleteUserTargetsTx` reached from `(*DB).DeleteUser` `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29`. Identical in `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102,380,400` and `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102,417,437`. Entry point `Store.DeleteUser` — `store/user.go:171-180`.
- Schema checked: `reaction` table has no `FOREIGN KEY` at all (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`); the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the whole schema is `memo_share.memo_id → memo(id)` (`sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`, `postgres/LATEST.sql:108`, `mysql/LATEST.sql:108`).

---

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is **no Redis** in this codebase — no `redis` dependency in `go.mod`, and no `redis` identifier anywhere in the Go sources. Actual mechanism: a process-local, in-memory cache — `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` struct `:65`, `New` `:74`, TTL-based `item.expiration` `:34-38`). `Store` holds three instances: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (`store/store.go:27-29`, constructed `store/store.go:51-53`). Config is hardcoded in `store.New` — `store/store.go:39-44`: `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`. So **user entries: 10-minute TTL** (`userCache`, populated at `store/user.go:143,167`, invalidated explicitly on update/delete via `store/user_delete.go:39-46`). Nothing is configurable at runtime, and nothing is shared across processes. (Separately, `APIV1Service.instanceStatsCache` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:44` — is its own small in-process memoization.)

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is **no per-user API rate-limiting middleware** in this codebase, so there are no request limits to report. Evidence: the only Echo middleware registered on the root server is `middleware.Recover()` and `newCORSMiddleware(profile)` — `server/server.go:51-52`; the frontend adds only static-file and SPA-fallback middleware (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54,59`). A case-insensitive search for `ratelimit`/`rate_limit`/`RateLimiter`/`throttle` across all Go files returns nothing, and no rate-limiter dependency exists in `go.mod`. The Connect/gateway interceptors (`server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`, `v1.go:64-85`) do auth/ACL only. The closest things that exist are concurrency caps, not rate limits: `semaphore.NewWeighted(3)` for thumbnail generation and `NewWeighted(2)` for image processing (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:60-61`), and the 128-slot bounded webhook dispatch queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:40`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is **no nightly database-cleanup job, and no cron scheduler running at all**. The `internal/scheduler` package (cron parser + job registry, `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:54`, `parser.go:ParseCronExpression`) exists but is never used by the server — the only references to `scheduler.New`/`Register` outside the package are in its own doc comment (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:12-32`) and its tests (`internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`, `example_test.go`). No cron expression is registered anywhere in production code. The only periodic background work is the S3 presign refresh on a 12-hour `time.Ticker` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41`, wired at `server/server.go:162-171`), plus the in-memory cache's 5-minute cleanup sweep (`store/store.go:41`).

**r04** — Premise is wrong on both counts: there is **no message broker** — neither NATS nor RabbitMQ/AMQP appears in `go.mod`, `go.sum`, or any Go file — and therefore no queue is declared anywhere. Actual mechanism: an in-process Go channel. `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:40`; four worker goroutines are started in the package `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-52`) and each drains the channel by calling `Post` (`:44`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`), which does a non-blocking send and **drops** the payload with a warning when the buffer is full (`:190-196`). The queue is unpersisted and per-process: pending deliveries are lost on restart, and there is no retry.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is **no GraphQL schema** — no `graphql`/`gqlgen` dependency and no `.graphql`/schema definition anywhere in the repo. The actual public API surface is **Protobuf-defined RPC**, served two ways from the same `*APIV1Service` implementation:
- Schema source: `proto/api/v1/*.proto` — `memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `common.proto`; generated Go in `proto/gen/api/v1/` (Connect stubs in `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/`).
- Connect RPC handlers registered at `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go:31-45`; gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON transcoding registered by `(*APIV1Service).RegisterGateway` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:64` (via `*.pb.gw.go`), with an embedded OpenAPI doc (`proto/openapi_embed.go`).
- Non-RPC HTTP surfaces alongside it: the file server (`/file/...`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), SSE (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`), `/healthz` (`server/server.go:64`), and MCP (`server/router/mcp/service.go`, wired at `server/server.go:91-95`).
